summary: STORM-style multi-perspective audit of the daily competitor pricing monitor outputs

audits.perspective: Pricing PM who sets monthly PAYG price steps against a standing band: floor = Nebius reserve x1.6, cap = cheapest hyperscaler x0.97, anchor = peer median +5%, gated on demand signals. Reads the artifacts to pull band inputs, judge median trust, and spot triggered/blocked steps and market direction.

questions.q: Can I read off today's cap input (cheapest like-for-like hyperscaler on-demand) per SKU without hunting?
questions.evidence: Slack thread: 'vs cheapest hyperscaler on-demand (8xSXM cluster, like-for-like): H100 Nebius $3.85 vs AWS $6.88'; Confluence Executive Benchmark has a 'Cheapest hyperscaler (on-demand)' column per GPU with SXM tags.
questions.uncertainty: The input is cheapest-region list price (AWS US $6.88 vs Europe $8.94 in the regional table); the footnote itself says enterprise customers pay 40-57% less at 3yr committed, so a x0.97 cap on list is generous. The basis is stated but the reader must know their rule uses list.
questions.fix: In the Decision Triggers (or a new Band Inputs) table, add a computed 'cap = cheapest hyperscaler x0.97 -> $X' cell per SKU with the region basis named, so the cap is a number, not arithmetic.

questions.q: Can I read off today's anchor input (peer median in $) per SKU?
questions.evidence: Slack thread gives only the relative view ('H100 Nebius $3.85 -4% vs median') - the median dollar value never appears in Slack and must be back-computed. Confluence does carry 'Enterprise peer median' ($3.99 / $6.15 / $8.39 / $9.01), but it sits mid-table in the Executive Benchmark, and for B300 the 'median' is effectively one provider (Scaleway $9.01).
questions.uncertainty: Whether the Confluence median column uses the same cluster-only peer set as the Slack lines (see next question - the peer counts disagree), so back-computing anchor = median x1.05 from either artifact may give different answers.
questions.fix: Print the median dollar value and its n inline in the Slack thread peer lines ('-4% vs median $3.99 (n=3)') and add an 'anchor = median +5% -> $X' computed column to Confluence.

questions.q: Do I trust the peer median: how many peers, is n consistent, is the basis clean?
questions.evidence: The two artifacts contradict each other on n. Slack thread H100: '0/3 peers cheaper'; Confluence H100: 'Enterprise peers tracked: 4'. Slack thread B300: '1 peer: Scaleway $9.01' with the % deliberately suppressed; Confluence B300 shows '-13% vs median' in green with 'peers tracked: 2'. So the page displays a median-based verdict the thread refuses to show, and the n shown next to the median ('tracked') is not the n the median was computed over (code: _position_for_tier dedupes to cluster-only peers; the 'tracked' registry count includes non-cluster SKUs).
questions.uncertainty: The cluster-class filter itself is sound (_is_cluster_peer gates on 8xSXM; docs say so on the page) and freshness is banner-visible ('14/14 sources live'). The defect is confined to n-labeling and an inconsistent minimum-n rule, not the price data - but an anchor at +5% on an n=2 median (H200: Together $5.99, CoreWeave $6.30) is noise-sensitive and nothing flags that.
questions.fix: One min-n rule enforced in both generators (suppress or grey the % when median n<3 everywhere, including Confluence B300), and rename/split the Confluence column into 'in median (n)' vs 'tracked' so the displayed n matches the computation.

questions.q: Can I read off the floor input (Nebius reserve/committed price) and how fresh it is?
questions.evidence: Nebius committed tiers are on the page (H100 1yr $2.30 / 2yr $2.05, 'Committed list verified 2026-06-23') but four sections deep in Committed Pricing Comparison, and the floor itself (reserve x1.6) is never computed. Today the verification is 13 days old with no aging alarm.
questions.uncertainty: Which tier the PM's rule means by 'reserve' (enterprise 512+ 100%-upfront shown, standard tier ~5-10% higher per footnote) - the artifact shows both bases exist but doesn't say which one the band rule keys off.
questions.fix: Surface the Nebius committed reference price (named tier) in the Band Inputs table with 'floor = reserve x1.6 -> $X' as static-formula text, plus a visible warning when committed-list verification age exceeds ~30 days.

questions.q: Do I see when a price step is triggered or blocked?
questions.evidence: The Decision Triggers table stops at qualitative actions: 'Headroom to hold or raise', 'Hold; monitor', with Owner/Review-by/Margin-risk as permanent em-dash placeholders. Nowhere is the gap to anchor quantified (H200 $4.50 vs anchor $6.46 = median $6.15 x1.05 implies a step candidate) and the demand gate is never mentioned, so a step can be neither confirmed triggered nor explicitly blocked.
questions.uncertainty: The demand gate genuinely cannot be computed in GitHub Actions (no DWH access), so 'triggered' can only ever be 'step candidate pending internal demand check' - the fix must stay static-text on the gate.
questions.fix: Add a computed 'vs anchor' column per SKU (Nebius OD vs peer-median x1.05, % gap, status: step candidate / in band / above cap) plus one static sentence: 'Step execution is demand-gated - confirm NER/sell-through internally before moving.'

questions.q: Is market direction visible - 7-day and 30-day trend per SKU?
questions.evidence: Only a 30d cell exists ('Market 30d: +0% / 30d' on every row) and the Slack action flags render it with a duplicated label: 'H200 Headroom to hold or raise | 30d +0% / 30d' (diff.py _format_action_flags_thread prepends '30d ' to a trend string that already ends '/ 30d'). There is no 7d trend anywhere, and per _market_trend the series tracks only the current cheapest peer's own on-demand price - not the median the anchor is built on; history is <90d so cells read 'building' or +0%.
questions.uncertainty: History depth (~1 month per code comments) limits what any trend can show today; +0% across all five SKUs may be real market flatness or just a floor-provider that hasn't moved.
questions.fix: Track the peer-median series per SKU in history and show '7d / 30d' for it (falls out of the same CSV), and fix the label to 'mkt +0%/30d' in the Slack flags.

questions.q: When an anchor or cap input actually moves, will the delta-first post tell me in band terms?
questions.evidence: The 'Price moves >=3%' section lists raw provider moves - today 2 of 3 are 1Legion ('small provider'), which is not in the enterprise peer set and thus irrelevant to the anchor; the one relevant move (AWS H200 spot +4.4%) touches neither the OD cap nor the peer median. No line ever says 'peer median for X moved -> anchor now $Y' or 'cheapest hyperscaler changed -> cap now $Z'.
questions.uncertainty: Today is genuinely quiet, so absence of a band-event line is not proof the logic is missing - but the code path (significant-diff grouping in format_slack_message) has no median/cap recompute hook, confirming it would stay silent on a Lambda cluster-price cut that shifts the H100 anchor.
questions.fix: Add a derived alert to the delta-first message: whenever the recomputed peer median or cheapest-hyperscaler price for a revenue-driver SKU changes >=2% day-over-day, lead with 'Band input moved: H100 peer median $3.99 -> $3.79, anchor now $3.98'.

questions.q: Are the spot/preemptible references sound enough to sanity-check the PVM/preemptible tier against?
questions.evidence: Slack thread spot section uses cheapest provider's median across zones with the phantom-floor guard ('single-zone dips excluded'); the spot/auction page adds a per-SKU 'Market floor reference' (H100 $1.80, B300 $3.50) with an honest read-me-first warning that field-intel deals are often committed, not pure spot.
questions.uncertainty: Thin bases are disclosed but easy to miss: 'AWS $2.85 (median, 1 zones)' for B200 and '(median, 1 zones)' for B300 - a one-zone 'median' is a single print, and the grammar bug ('1 zones') slightly undermines confidence in the machinery.
questions.fix: When n_zones = 1, label it 'single zone - low confidence' instead of '(median, 1 zones)', and fix the pluralization.

top_fixes: Add a per-SKU 'Pricing band inputs' table (top of Confluence + Monday thread): Nebius OD, floor = Nebius committed x1.6, anchor = peer median x1.05 (median $ and n shown), cap = cheapest hyperscaler x0.97, % gap to anchor, and a status column (step candidate pending internal demand gate / in band / above cap). All computable from public scraped prices plus the static formula - no DWH needed.

Make the peer median trustworthy and consistent: show the median dollar value with its true n in every artifact, make the Confluence 'peers tracked' column equal the median's computation basis (or split into 'in median' vs 'tracked'), and enforce one min-n rule so B300 stops showing '-13% vs median' on the page while the thread says '1 peer'.

Upgrade trend and change detection for band inputs: track the peer-median series per SKU and show 7d/30d for it, fix the duplicated '30d +0% / 30d' label in Slack action flags, and add a delta-first alert line whenever the peer median or cheapest-hyperscaler price moves >=2% ('band input moved, anchor/cap now $X').

audits.perspective: Finance / revenue owner: uses the daily pack to benchmark Nebius reserve/committed prices against competitor committed deals, size deal-loss economics, and trust that every displayed delta is on one auditable basis (term, prepay, volume tier, VAT/FX, consistent denominators).

questions.q: Do the headline 'lowest committed deal' prices and deal counts tie out to the field-intel evidence table on the same page?
questions.evidence: Summary table: 'B300 lowest $3.50 (3yr, 0%) via Azure [21 deals]', 'GB300 lowest $3.09 (60mo, 100%) [20 deals]', 'GB200 $4.75 [1 deals]'. The 'Field Intelligence — Recent Market Quotes' detail tables contain NO $3.50 Azure B300 row (12 rows shown vs 21 claimed), NO $3.09 GB300 row (11 rows vs 20), and no GB200 section at all. Root cause confirmed in code: detail table uses _load_intel(days=60) (diff.py:1210) while summary/triggers use 90d (diff.py:403, 433, 1417, 2172). Headline lows dated 61-90 days ago are invisible in the evidence table.
questions.fix: Unify the window: pass days=90 in _build_field_intel_callout (diff.py:1210), or if 60d detail is deliberate, print the window on both tables ('lowest in 90d' vs 'quotes, last 60d') and tag out-of-window headline lows with their date. Counts and 'lowest' must come from the same filtered set the reader can see.
questions.uncertainty: Window mismatch is confirmed in code; whether a row cap also drops rows was not verified. The $3.50 Azure deal itself is sales-reported and cannot be independently verified.

questions.q: When the pack says a competitor committed deal is X% below our committed price, is the comparison like-for-like on prepay and structure?
questions.evidence: Slack bottom line: 'competitors quoting B300 from $3.50 vs our $4.55 (-23%)' compares a 0%-prepay Azure deal to Nebius's 100%-upfront, 512+ GPU tier with no flag; every field-intel summary row does the same ('H100 lowest $1.80 (1yr, 0%) ... -22% vs Nebius $2.30' where $2.30 is all-upfront enterprise). The page itself states the rule it breaks: 'A like-for-like comparison should match prepay terms — the all-upfront vs no-upfront gap is ~2x on AWS 3yr.' Since 100%-upfront is our deepest rate, the displayed deltas UNDERSTATE the competitive gap.
questions.fix: Annotate every 'vs Nebius committed' delta with the basis ('vs our 100%-upfront 512+ tier; deal is 0% prepay — like-for-like gap wider') and add Nebius's 0%/30%-upfront tier prices as a column (the prose says these tiers exist). In the Slack bottom line, add the one-clause flag. Static text, no new data needed.
questions.uncertainty: Nebius 0%-prepay rates are internal, not in the artifacts, so I cannot quantify how much the -23% understates the true gap.

questions.q: Are the peer-median deltas ('-4% vs median', '0/3 peers cheaper') computed on a stated, consistent denominator across Slack and Confluence?
questions.evidence: Confluence exec table intro says 'On-demand prices, cheapest available per provider', yet shows Lambda H100 at $3.99 while the same page's Complete Market Sweep shows Lambda at $3.29 (1x GPU, -15% vs Nebius) — the exec table silently filters to cluster-class 8x-node pricing (only the Slack thread says 'cluster-class like-for-like'). Registry peers Voltage Park ($1.99), GMI ($2.00), Hyperstack ($2.50) sell H100 below Nebius $3.85 in the sweep while the headline says '0/3 peers cheaper'. Counts also disagree: thread 'H200 0/2 peers cheaper' vs Confluence '3 peers tracked'; thread 'B300 1 peer' vs Confluence '2 peers tracked' with '-13% vs median' where the 'median' is a single provider (Scaleway $9.01).
questions.fix: Change the exec-table caption to 'cluster-class (8x SXM node) list price per provider; single-GPU prices in the sweep below'; emit one peer count per SKU (peers with a current cluster-class price) reused by both formatters; render 'vs only priced peer' instead of 'vs median' when n=1.
questions.uncertainty: The 8x-node filter is inferred from the numbers (Lambda 1x $3.29 vs cluster $3.99); the exact _is_cluster_peer rule in diff.py:221 may differ in detail.

questions.q: Is the lost B300 deal economically sized (GPUs, term, contract value) so I can weigh a committed-price move against the revenue actually at stake?
questions.evidence: Slack: 'B300 lost a deal at the field price. Review committed pricing for this SKU.' Decision Trigger: '$3.50 (3yr, Azure) lost deal'. No GPU count, no TCV, and it is ambiguous which deal was lost — the only detail row marked as a loss is a different price ('2026-06-12 Undisclosed hyperscaler $3.80 3yr — competitive B300 win vs Nebius'); the $3.50 Azure row is not shown at all (see Q1). Other intel rows carry sizes (e.g. '576 GPUs', '4k B300s'), so the CSV supports this.
questions.fix: Carry deal size from the intel CSV into the flag and headline: 'lost N GPUs x 3yr at their $3.50 = ~$X contract value' (N x 3.50 x 24 x 365 x 3 is computable in the generator); print 'size not reported' when absent; state the date/provider of the triggering deal so it matches one evidence row.
questions.uncertainty: The triggering deal's size may genuinely be absent from the CSV; then the honest fix is displaying 'size unreported', not implying precision.

questions.q: When a field deal has a stated cluster size, is it compared against the Nebius tier that size would actually get?
questions.evidence: Committed section: figures are 'enterprise tier (512+ GPUs), 100% upfront — the most aggressive available rate. Standard tier (<512 GPU) is ~5-10% higher.' The AWS field deal is a '232-GPU cluster' yet is compared to the 512+ tier: '-22% vs Nebius $2.30'. At standard tier (~$2.42-2.53) the real gap is roughly -26 to -29%. The caveat exists in prose but no delta applies it.
questions.fix: Where the intel row states GPU count <512, compute the delta against standard tier (enterprise price x 1.05-1.10) and label it, or footnote the summary table: 'deltas vs 512+ tier; sub-512 deals compare ~5-10% worse'.
questions.uncertainty: Standard-tier uplift is a range (5-10%), so corrected deltas are ranges; the exact tier ladder is internal.

questions.q: Are spot comparisons on one stated basis (median across zones vs cheapest zone), without a same-page contradiction an auditor could catch?
questions.evidence: Thread footnote: 'floors are the cheapest provider's median across zones (single-zone dips excluded)' sits directly above 'B200 ... AWS $2.85 (median, 1 zones)' and 'B300 ... AWS $4.44 (median, 1 zones)' — a 1-zone 'median' IS a single-zone reading. And the Slack summary's 'our $2.15 vs Azure spot $2.27 (median) (-5%)' coexists with the battlecard/regional table showing Azure best-zone H100 spot at $1.40 (35% below us).
questions.fix: When zone count is 1, render 'single zone — low confidence' instead of '(median, 1 zones)'; in the Slack reference line show both numbers: 'vs Azure spot $2.27 (median, 21 zones; best zone $1.40)'. The spot/auction page's 'Read me first' panel is the right model.
questions.uncertainty: Median-across-zones is arguably the right anchor for PVM floor-setting; the issue is presentation consistency, not the methodology choice.

questions.q: Is the currency and tax basis stated (USD, ex-VAT, FX conversion for EUR-listed providers like Scaleway)?
questions.evidence: Header says only 'All prices in $/GPU-hr'. No ex-VAT statement anywhere in any artifact; Scaleway (EUR public list) appears as $9.01 / $3.30 / $1.70 with no FX rate or date, so an auditor reproducing from Scaleway's site would get a different number and no explanation.
questions.fix: Add one static header line: 'All prices USD, excl. VAT/taxes; non-USD list prices converted by the source (ComputePrices.com) / at [rate, date]'. Static text is allowed under the GitHub-Actions constraint.
questions.uncertainty: Conversion may happen upstream in ComputePrices.com at an unknown rate; if so the note should attribute the source rather than claim a rate.

questions.q: Is every displayed number dated or freshness-flagged so nothing stale is silently presented as today's price?
questions.evidence: 'Data freshness: 14/14 sources live — all sources live this run'; 'Nebius committed list verified 2026-06-23'; AWS Capacity Blocks 'verified June 2026'; every field-intel row individually dated; 30d trend cells label their real span. This is the pack's strongest audit property.
questions.fix: None required. Nice-to-have: on cache-fallback days, a per-provider 'as-of' date next to affected prices (the health line already exists as the hook).
questions.uncertainty: Today is an all-live run, so I could not observe how a cache-fallback day renders; the safeguard is asserted by the badge, not demonstrated.

top_fixes: Unify the field-intel windows so headlines tie to evidence: change _load_intel(days=60) to days=90 in _build_field_intel_callout (diff.py:1210) or label both windows explicitly — today the lost-deal $3.50 Azure B300, the $3.09 GB300, and the deal counts (21 vs 12 rows) cannot be verified on the page that cites them.

Flag the prepay/tier basis on every 'vs Nebius committed' delta (Slack bottom line included): deltas currently compare competitors' 0%-prepay deals to Nebius's 100%-upfront 512+ tier, understating the gap; add the basis clause and, where deal size <512 GPUs, compare against standard tier (+5-10%).

Make peer-median denominators consistent and honest: correct the exec-table caption from 'cheapest available per provider' to 'cluster-class (8x-node) list price', use one peer count per SKU across Slack and Confluence, and never label an n=1 comparison as a 'median'.

audits.perspective: PVM Auctions designer (Q4 project, RFC 055): needs competitor spot price distributions, bid-mechanism intel, interruption terms, a defensible floor/target anchor, and volatility over time — not just today's minima.

questions.q: What is the competitor spot price DISTRIBUTION per GPU (median, spread across providers/zones), not just the cheapest number, so I can place an auction target inside the market range?
questions.evidence: spot_auction_body.html shows one point estimate per signal per GPU ('Cheapest hyperscaler spot (median across zones): $2.27 (Azure)'). The distribution partially exists on the OTHER page: confluence_body.html Regional Comparison shows H100 spot Azure US $1.40 / EU $1.55 / APAC $2.28, GCP $2.05/$3.81/$2.76, AWS $3.91 — but only cheapest-per-geo, no percentiles, and the spot page never links to it.
questions.fix: On the spot/auction page add a per-provider row set per GPU: median + min–max across zones for AWS/GCP/Azure (data already scraped — Azure H100 has 21 zone observations), plus SF Compute. All computable from existing PriceRecords in _representative_spot_floor's by_prov dict; expose the full prov_median map instead of only min().
questions.uncertainty: Zone-level scrape coverage varies by GPU (B200/B300 have 1 zone each), so 'distribution' for B-series will honestly be a single point — the fix should show n per provider rather than imply spread that isn't there.

questions.q: Who actually runs a real bid/auction mechanism for GPUs, and what is the mechanism (true auction vs provider-set price with a max-price cap)?
questions.evidence: The two artifacts contradict each other. confluence_body.html Product-Model Gaps: 'Bid / max-price spot — AWS: Yes, GCP: No, Azure: Yes'. spot_auction_body.html note: 'Azure is the only major cloud with GPU spot bidding'. Neither describes the mechanism itself (AWS max-price is a cap on an algorithmically set price, not a bid auction since 2017; SF Compute is an order-book exchange).
questions.fix: Reconcile the two pages and add a short static 'mechanism' column on the spot page: AWS = provider-set price + user max-price cap (no auction); Azure = same (eviction on price or capacity); GCP = fixed preemptible discount, no bids; SF Compute = order-book market. Static text is fine under the GitHub Actions constraint.
questions.uncertainty: Whether Azure's max-price counts as 'bidding' is a definitional call; either definition is defensible, but the two pages must use the same one. CoreWeave/neocloud mechanisms are '—' (unverified), not 'No'.

questions.q: What are competitors' interruption terms — eviction notice period, eviction trigger (price vs capacity), max runtime, restart policy — so I can design PVM interruption terms competitively?
questions.evidence: The only interruption language anywhere is the caveat 'Hyperscaler spot is interruptible, capacity not guaranteed' (slack_thread.txt line 23, repeated on both Confluence pages). No notice periods (AWS 2-min, GCP 30-sec, Azure 30-sec), no eviction-trigger detail, nothing on Nebius preemptible's own terms.
questions.fix: Add a static interruption-terms table to the spot/auction page (provider | notice period | eviction trigger | capacity guarantee | source link). This is stable public documentation, needs no daily compute, and is exactly what an auction-terms section of RFC 055 must cite.
questions.uncertainty: Provider terms change occasionally; the table needs a 'verified <date>' stamp like the committed-list one ('Nebius committed list verified 2026-06-23') so staleness is visible.

questions.q: Does the 'Market floor reference' give me a floor anchor I can defend in the RFC?
questions.evidence: spot_auction_body.html defines it as 'the lowest real competitor spot/auction signal observed (hyperscaler spot median, SF Compute market price, or a field-intel deal)' — but the bolded H100 floor $1.80 is a 1yr COMMITTED deal and the B300 floor $3.50 is a 3yr committed deal, not spot clears. The caveat ('often committed rather than pure spot') is honest but the headline min() erases it.
questions.fix: Split the column in two: 'Spot-clearing anchor' = min(hyperscaler spot median, SF Compute) — H100 $2.04, H200 $2.17, B200 $2.85, B300 $4.44 — and 'Negotiated committed floor (term)' = field-intel lowest with term shown. Add one static line tying to the PRD floor rule (floor = 1/3 PAYG → H100 $1.28) alongside the existing ~$0.40 cost floor so all three candidate floors sit on one line.
questions.uncertainty: Whether a 3yr-committed $3.50 belongs anywhere near a spot floor is a modeling judgment; some designers want the absolute willingness-to-pay floor. Keeping both columns preserves that choice instead of pre-deciding it via min().

questions.q: How volatile are competitor spot prices over time (30d range), so the floor survives typical dips and I can pick a repricing cadence?
questions.evidence: No time-series appears on the spot/auction page at all. The only trend anywhere is 'Market 30d = change in the cheapest enterprise-peer ON-DEMAND price' (confluence_body.html, +0% on every GPU) and today's single move (slack: 'AWS raised H200 spot +4% ($1.71→$1.78)'). Yet store/history.csv holds ~8,930 rows of daily zone-level spot snapshots since 2026-05-15 (~7 weeks) — the volatility is computable from data the tool already has.
questions.fix: Add a 30d volatility row per GPU on the spot page: min / median / max of the daily hyperscaler-spot-floor and of SF Compute over the trailing 30d, from history.csv. Pure public-scrape computation, fits the GitHub Actions constraint.
questions.uncertainty: History only reaches back to 2026-05-15 and early snapshots mixed in coverage backfill (diff.py line ~1354 notes contamination), so the first volatility read needs a 'span: Xd' label like the existing trend cells.

questions.q: Are the floor signals like-for-like with a PVM auction product (interruptible, per-GPU-hr, no term), or is the field-intel column contaminated by term-committed deals?
questions.evidence: _field_intel_floor (diff.py:1404) takes the lowest 90d deal regardless of consumption type — B300 floor $3.50 is '3yr, 0%' committed; intel.csv even contains a spot-comparable B300 signal (BoostRun $3.80 On-demand, 2026-06-04, unconfirmed) that loses the min() to a 3yr deal. The disclosure exists ('field-intel deals are sales-reported and often committed, not pure spot') but the number the reader will copy is the contaminated one.
questions.fix: In _field_intel_floor, split by term: report lowest on-demand/short-term (<=3mo) deal separately from lowest committed deal; the intel CSV already carries term_months, so this is a filter, not new data.
questions.uncertainty: Field-intel rows are sales-reported and anonymized ('lower confidence than published list prices'); a term split shrinks n per bucket — B-series short-term buckets may often be empty, which is itself useful signal.

questions.q: How reliable is each floor signal — zone counts, phantom-price filtering, SF Compute price basis, deal counts and dates?
questions.evidence: Zone counts appear in Slack ('AWS $2.85 (median, 1 zones)') but are dropped from the spot page's floor table. The B200 'floor' $2.85 is a single-zone price sitting 79.99% below AWS's own $14.24 on-demand — it passes the tool's own phantom filter (MAX_SPOT_DISCOUNT = 0.80 in diff.py:188) by 0.01pp, while the code comment says genuine spot discounts run ~60-70%. SF Compute '$2.04' has no contract-duration basis or date; the field-intel cell shows no deal count or date (main page shows '21 deals' for B300, spot page doesn't).
questions.fix: Carry n_zones (already returned by _representative_spot_floor), field-intel deal count + date, and an SF Compute duration/date basis into the spot page table; flag single-zone or near-phantom-threshold signals explicitly (e.g. 'B200: 1 zone, at 80% below own OD — treat as indicative only'). Also fix the '1 zones' plural in Slack.
questions.uncertainty: Whether AWS's B200 spot at 80% below own OD is phantom or a real early-capacity price is unknowable from scrapes alone; the fix is to surface the ambiguity, not resolve it.

questions.q: Where does Nebius preemptible sit vs the market today, per GPU?
questions.evidence: slack_thread.txt lines 18-21 and the spot page column give it cleanly: H100 $2.15 (5% below Azure spot median), H200 $2.45 (13% above AWS), B200 $3.95 (39% above AWS), B300 $4.30 (3% below AWS) — with the '% of what' basis stated (median across zones, cheapest hyperscaler).
questions.fix: Only refinement: annotate that the B200 '+39% above' comparator is the single-zone near-phantom $2.85 (see Q7), so the positioning read on B200 is soft.
questions.uncertainty: The B200/B300 comparisons rest on 1 zone each; the H100/H200 reads (21 and 4 zones) are solid.

top_fixes: Split the spot page's 'Market floor reference' into two columns — spot-clearing anchor (hyperscaler spot median + SF Compute only) vs negotiated committed floor (field intel, term shown) — and stop min()-ing across mechanisms; add one static line placing the three candidate floors side by side (competitor spot clear, 1/3-PAYG PRD rule ≈ $1.28 for H100, ~$0.40 cost floor).

Add a 30d spot volatility block per GPU (min/median/max of the daily hyperscaler spot floor and SF Compute) computed from store/history.csv (~7 weeks of zone-level snapshots already collected) — the designer needs the range a floor must survive, not a point estimate.

Carry reliability metadata into the spot table (n_zones, field-intel deal count + date, SF Compute duration basis) and flag near-phantom signals — the B200 floor $2.85 is a single-zone price at 79.99% below AWS's own on-demand, passing the tool's 80% phantom filter by 0.01pp; also reconcile the bid-mechanism contradiction (Product-Model Gaps says AWS bid spot = Yes; spot page says Azure is the only cloud with GPU spot bidding) and add a static interruption-terms table (notice period, eviction trigger).

still_missed: Self-move attribution: no perspective asks whether the pack distinguishes 'we moved' from 'the market moved'. Every delta ('-4% vs median', 'Changed in 24h', 30d trend) silently shifts when Nebius changes its own list price, which is imminent (July-6 proposal: H200/B200/B300 +5%). Under delta-first cadence a self-caused position change would read as market news. Cheap to compute: nebius rows are already in the diff; add one 'Nebius price change today' line and tag position deltas as self-caused when nebius appears in diffs.

Action-flag lifecycle: the B300 'lost deal' flag has no state, no age, and no retirement rule; it re-fires every post until the intel row ages past 90d, then vanishes silently. Nobody asks how a pricing decision ('reviewed, holding premium') acknowledges and silences a flag, or how flag age is shown. Under the new cadence a standing flag repeated every Monday trains execs to ignore the one channel signal that matters.

House-style compliance: none of the seven verified the 48-char Slack table limit. Thread peer rows run ~80 chars (e.g. 'H100 Nebius $3.85 -4% vs median | 0/3 peers cheaper | floor: Lambda $3.99') and wrap on mobile/sidebar, destroying the aligned columns the format depends on. The owner's own hard constraint is currently violated by the flagship table.

Confidentiality governance of the pages themselves: the Field Intelligence section claims 'customer names removed' yet rows name counterparties and deal specifics (HUMAIN 4k B300s London, Anyscale 92 nodes, LAI ~5k B200, BoostRun 20k, Pale Blue Dot 1600x GB300). No perspective asks who can view the Confluence page, whether competitor negotiated-deal intel on a broadly readable wiki needs a legal/compliance pass, or what the handling rule is beyond the sales AE's 'do not quote externally' label.

Win-side selection bias: field intel logs only competitor quotes and losses; there is no 'deals we won at $X' signal, so the pack structurally over-reports price pressure (#price-intelligence is where AEs post scary quotes). No perspective questioned the evidence base's bias or asked for a win/loss balance line next to the lost-deal flag.

Inference/per-token reader: the RTX PRO 6000 section was audited by nobody, and managed inference platforms (Together, fal, Deep Infra) are excluded by design with no pointer to where that comparison lives. A Token Factory / inference PM gets no verdict on whether $/GPU-hr is even the right frame for that competitive surface.
conflicts: Pricing PM fix 1 (band-inputs table: floor = reserve x1.6, cap = cheapest hyperscaler x0.97, anchor = median x1.05) vs Sales AE fix 2 (confidentiality): it would publish Nebius's pricing formula to a channel read by sales and a broadly readable Confluence page, handing negotiation leverage to any customer who sees it. It also brushes the no-DWH constraint: the demand gate can never be computed, so 'step candidate pending internal gate' permanently reads as a recommendation without its gate. Resolution: restricted sub-page, or publish only the inputs (median $, n, cheapest hyperscaler $) without the multipliers.

Exec fix 3 (replace the H100-only spot line with the cross-SKU range '-5% H100 to +39% B200') vs Capacity fix 1 and PVM fix 3 (confidence-gate thin spot): the +39% B200 endpoint IS the single-zone price that passes the 80% phantom filter by 0.02pp (AWS $2.85 vs own OD $14.24 = 79.98% discount). Sequencing dependency: apply zone-count/phantom gating first, else the exec range institutionalizes the least trustworthy number in the pack.

Data-quality fix 2 (name-insensitive dedup, retire Undisclosed seeds) vs Sales/Finance accurate deal counts: a key-based rule over-collapses genuinely distinct rows (Verda + CIVO $4.25 is one joint offer via two providers) while missing named-vs-Undisclosed twins on different dates (HUMAIN $3.60 May-22 vs Undisclosed $3.60 May-22 would collapse, but a re-logged deal a week later would not). Correct dedup needs a curated superseded_by column in the manual CSV, which is re-curation work, not the cheap generator fix the audit implies.

Exec fix 2 (GB300 fallback: compare the lowest deal at a term Nebius offers) vs Finance fix 2 (one auditable basis per delta): the fallback inherently mixes prepay/term bases (e.g. the $3.09 headline is 60mo/100% upfront vs Nebius 3yr tiers). Both can ship only if the fallback row carries an explicit off-basis label, otherwise it violates the like-for-like rule Finance wants enforced everywhere.

Sales AE fix 1 (relabel exec benchmark 'cheapest cluster-class (8xSXM) per provider') vs the actual computation: _position_for_tier (diff.py:252-258) falls back to ALL peers when no SXM peer exists, which is exactly the case for B300 (Scaleway 8x, untagged) and L40S (PCIe everywhere). The proposed caption would be newly wrong for those rows; it must state the fallback ('cluster-class where available; PCIe basis for L40S; B300 has no SXM-tagged peer yet').

That is 'expensive', not the computed-from-data-in-hand fix the capacity audit presents it as; cluster size currently lives only in free-text notes.
